headline: Zoox upgrades robotaxi with enhanced comfort features ahead of commercial launch
summary: The Amazon-owned company has upgraded its custom-built robotaxi with rider feedback in mind.
details: The upgraded Zoox robotaxi features a refreshed interior design with more padding and ergonomic curves on the seats and headrests. The new color palette includes aloe green seating and stone grey flooring and trim, creating a calmer environment for riders.

The robotaxi also has improved visibility with relocated bidirectional reflectors, a new speaker and microphone for better communication, and a more visible touchscreen. Additionally, the charging pad has been updated with fluting to keep phones in place, and the cupholders have been enlarged.

The company is preparing for commercial service, with a production facility in Hayward, California, capable of producing up to 10,000 robotaxis per year. Zoox is awaiting a decision from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration for a commercial exemption.

The robotaxi can transport four people at speeds of up to 75 miles per hour and features 40 cameras, radars, lidars, and infrared sensors to perceive its environment. It still lacks a steering wheel and other controls, and drives bidirectionally with four-wheel steering.

headline_marked: OpenAI unveils [[custom AI chip Jalapeño]] with Broadcom
headline: OpenAI unveils custom AI chip Jalapeño with Broadcom
summary: OpenAI's first custom-built inference processor, Jalapeño, boosts performance-per-watt.
details: OpenAI has unveiled its first custom-built inference processor, Jalapeño, developed in collaboration with Broadcom. The chip is designed to improve performance-per-watt for OpenAI's AI models.

Jalapeño is specifically designed for inference, the process of running pre-built AI models in response to user commands. OpenAI emphasized the chip's low operating cost when running real-time coding models.
The partnership was officially announced in October, as part of OpenAI's efforts to reduce dependence on Nvidia's GPUs. Google and Amazon have also built custom chips for similar purposes.
OpenAI's AI models assisted in the development of Jalapeño, which is still being tested. Early results show significantly better performance-per-watt than current state-of-the-art alternatives.
